items.topic: Thomas Midgley Jr. — leaded gasoline and Freon
items.title: One Chemist Poisoned the Air Twice
items.hook: Thomas Midgley added lead to gasoline to stop engines knocking, then invented Freon to stop refrigerators killing people. Both worked. Both went global. He died in a machine of his own design, strangled by the pulley that lifted his polio-crippled body out of bed.
items.demand: Midgley is a Veritasium-class search: 'most damaging inventor' is a perennial query. Wikipedia holds and spikes whenever a climate or lead-pipe story trends. English cinematic 12-minute versions in this painted style do not exist.
items.why: Same form as Tambora→Frankenstein: one cause, two disasters, a personal ending. Every scene is a 1920s lab, a filling station, a sky.
items.gap: Talking-head essays and Wikipedia-readalouds own the slot. A hook-first painted cut does not.

items.title: They Held a Bomb Core Apart With a Screwdriver
items.hook: In 1946, Louis Slotin was showing visiting scientists how close a plutonium pit could get to going critical. The only thing between the two beryllium hemispheres was a flathead screwdriver. It slipped.
items.demand: Demon Core is a reliable curiosity query (nuclear, Manhattan, 'third eye' stories). Wendigoon-adjacent audience already watches it. Short, complete, viscerally visual — the screwdriver, the blue flash, the hospital.
items.why: Exactly the Icarus shape: one rule, one demonstration, one night. 8–12 minutes, no padding.
items.gap: Reddit lore and 40-minute documentaries. No Odyssey-voiced 12-minute painted version.

items.topic: Challenger — the night they launched anyway
items.title: The Engineers Said No. The Shuttle Went Up Anyway.
items.hook: The night before Challenger, Thiokol engineers recommended not launching below 53°F. It was 36°. Management overruled them. Seventy-three seconds later the O-rings that had been too cold to seal did what the memo said they would do.
items.demand: Challenger is a top-tier disaster query, seasonal around January 28 and any new NASA failure. Search is huge; the 'they launched anyway' causal cut is still thinner than anniversary montages.
items.why: A conference call is the Cyclops. The rubber ring is the wings. Same art form, 1986.
items.gap: News packages and 90-minute docs. Not a cinematic 12-minute thesis.

items.title: He Dated the Earth — Then They Tried to Bury Him
items.hook: Clair Patterson spent years in a white room to weigh the age of the planet: 4.55 billion. The number that would not go away was lead. It was in the ice, the ocean, and his own blood — because a company had put it in the gasoline.
items.demand: Patterson + tetraethyllead spikes with every lead-pipe and 'age of the Earth' cycle. Veritasium proved the appetite. Our differentiator is the painted lab, not a presenter in a warehouse.
items.why: Clean-room vs. smelter. Ice cores. A man vs. Ethyl Corporation. Visual as a myth.
items.gap: One famous talking-head video. The 'entire story' painted pack is open.

items.title: They Were Told to Sharpen the Brush With Their Lips
items.hook: Factory girls painting watch dials were taught to lip-point the brush. The paint was radium. Their bones began to glow. The company said they were hysterical — until a dead girl's bones lit up a laboratory.
items.demand: Radium Girls is a steady true-crime/history-of-science hybrid query. Strong female-lead search, strong thumbnail (glowing jaw, dark factory).
items.why: Matches dancing-plague energy: a workplace rule that was the disease. Painterly night interiors.
items.gap: Podcasts and a 2018 film. YouTube 'entire story explained' in this style is thin.

items.title: The Doctors Wouldn't Wash Their Hands
items.hook: In a Vienna maternity ward, women died of childbed fever after the doctors walked over from the autopsy room. Semmelweis made them wash in chlorine. Deaths collapsed. The hospital rejected him. He died of an infected wound in an asylum.
items.demand: Semmelweis is a medical-history evergreen, revived every pandemic. 'Handwashing' is one of the most searched public-health stories on Earth.
items.why: The Broad-Street-pump shape: one ward, one rule, one man nobody believed. Dark Vault voice, science pictures.
items.gap: TED-adjacent lectures. Not a 12-minute tragedy with a thesis.

items.title: The Man Who Did Not End the World
items.hook: The satellite said American missiles were in the air. Protocol said report it. Petrov looked at the screen, decided the machine was lying, and did not pick up the phone.
items.demand: Petrov spikes every 'close calls' roundup and every nuclear-news cycle. High CTR title. Cold-war teal lighting is built for this channel's look.
items.why: One night, one screen, one refusal. The entire story fits 8 minutes without cheating.
items.gap: Shorts and list videos. A full painted scene-pack of Serpukhov-15 is open.

items.title: They Polished It Perfectly — To the Wrong Shape
items.hook: The Hubble mirror was the most precise thing anyone had ground. It was also 2.2 microns too flat. The error was in the test instrument that told them they were done. For three years the most expensive telescope in history could not see.
items.demand: Hubble is a monster astronomy query; 'Hubble repair' and spherical aberration still search. JWST news recycles the audience.
items.why: A perfect mistake. Space, clean rooms, the 1993 astronauts with a corrective lens. Visual paradise.
items.gap: NASA PR and long docs. The causal 12-minute cut ('the test lied') is the opening we own.

items.title: They Demoted Her. Then Her Letters Saved Millions.
items.hook: Katalin Karikó spent decades being rejected, demoted, and moved to a basement office for insisting that messenger RNA could become medicine. The modification nobody funded became the COVID vaccines. The Nobel arrived in 2023.
items.demand: Karikó + mRNA is still a high-volume search three years after the Nobel. Health, immigrant-scientist, and 'they laughed at her' audiences overlap.
items.why: Same lesson as Icarus inverted: the invention was not believed. Painted labs, fluorescent benches, a woman at a desk with a grant stamped no.
items.gap: News profiles. Not an entire-story cinematic explainer with scene cards.

items.title: The Sun Set the Telegraph Office on Fire
items.hook: On 1 September 1859 Richard Carrington watched a flare burst on the sun. Hours later, telegraph systems sparked, paper caught, and some operators kept sending with the batteries disconnected — the line was being powered by the sky.
items.demand: Carrington is a staple of 'solar storm' search, revived whenever NOAA posts an aurora watch. Prepper + science + history overlap is huge.
items.why: Last-three energy (one physical cause, civilization feels it). Auroras, brass instruments, a burning telegraph. Maps of the night side of Earth.
items.gap: Doomsday listicles. A precise 1859 story with a thesis is rarer.

items.title: He Became Immortal's Opposite — The ENTIRE Story of Gilgamesh
items.hook: The oldest story on earth exists because the gods built a wild man to humble a tyrant — then killed the friend, and sent a king walking to the end of the world for a plant he would lose in his sleep.
items.demand: 1.63M Wikipedia views in 12 months, rising (143K in Aug 2026). See U in History's Gilgamesh is 68× their average. A July 2026 'entire story' upload did 567K in a month. Search is hot; English cinematic 12-minute versions are thin.
items.why: Highest-upside epic in the niche that is not Odyssey. Flood tablet, Humbaba, Ishtar's rejection, Utnapishtim, the snake — every scene is a painting.
items.gap: Overserved as a 40-min lecture. Underserved as a hook-first 12-minute cut.

items.topic: The Aeneid — what happened to the Trojans who lived
items.title: Rome Exists Because One Trojan Refused to Die
items.hook: The Odyssey is the winner's way home. The Aeneid is the loser's: a man carrying his father out of a burning city founds an empire because he would not stay and burn with Troy.
items.demand: 909K Wikipedia views, sharply up (141K in Aug 2026 vs ~90K a year earlier). Odyssey itself is 9M — saturated. Aeneas rides the same search cluster with almost no 'ENTIRE Story of' clones.
items.why: Viewers who watched an Odyssey explainer are one click from 'what about the other side?' Dido, the underworld, the shield of Rome — visual as Homer.
items.gap: School summaries exist. A cinematic causal-hook version does not.

items.title: The Dragon Woke Because a Slave Stole a Cup
items.hook: Beowulf did not die fighting Grendel. He died as an old king because a terrified slave lifted one gold cup from a barrow, and a dragon that had slept three hundred years remembered it was owed.
items.demand: 1.13M Wikipedia views, steady ~88K/month. Always-on classroom + fantasy search. English 'entire story' videos skew academic or 3-hour sleep, not hook-first.
items.why: Three monsters, three ages of one man, one stolen cup. The ending is the lesson the format was built for.
items.gap: Everyone knows Grendel. Almost nobody leads with the cup.

items.title: A Kingdom Fell Because a King Kept One Promise to a Jealous Wife
items.hook: Fourteen years of exile, a kidnapped queen, and a war that burned Lanka happened because an aging king would not break a vow he should never have made.
items.demand: 1.30M Wikipedia views, rising (138K in Aug 2026). Massive global search; English cinematic explainers are far thinner than Hindi/Tamil ones. Diaspora + mythology YouTube is hungry.
items.why: Sita, Hanuman, Ravana, the golden deer — every beat is a 16:9 painting. Causal hook is Kaikeyi's boon, not 'good vs evil'.
items.gap: Devotional retells dominate. A dry, Odyssey-voiced causal cut is rare in English.

items.topic: Journey to the West — why Heaven couldn't kill the Monkey King
items.title: They Gave Him a Pilgrimage Because They Couldn't Kill Him
items.hook: Sun Wukong stormed heaven, erased his name from the book of the dead, and survived the furnace of the immortal. The journey for the scriptures was not a reward. It was the only prison that fit.
items.demand: 797K Wikipedia views, flat-high. Black Myth: Wukong (2024–26) dumped a new audience onto the 16th-century novel. Searchers want the original story, not the game.
items.why: Game traffic + 500-year-old plot + a trickster who cannot die. Visuals write themselves.
items.gap: Game lore videos own the query. The actual novel, told as one causal story, is open.

items.title: The Gods Walked Into the End of the World on Purpose
items.hook: Odin hung on the world-tree for nine nights to learn the runes, and what he learned was the date of his own death. Ragnarök is not a surprise. It is an appointment the gods kept.
items.demand: 527K Wikipedia views. Norse search is perennial (Thor, Loki, God of War). 'Entire story of Ragnarök' is crowded with listicles; the 'they knew' angle is not.
items.why: Fenrir, Jörmungandr, Baldur's mistletoe, the ship of nails — peak cinematic. The hook is knowledge, not spectacle.
items.gap: Marvel and God of War ate the surface. The Poetic Edda's fatalism is still unused.

items.title: The Queen of Heaven Walked Into Hell Naked on Purpose
items.hook: At each of seven gates they took a piece of her power — crown, beads, breastplate — until the goddess of love hung as a corpse on a hook. She had come to take her sister's throne.
items.demand: Inanna/Ishtar sits under Gilgamesh's search umbrella but has almost no English 'entire story' videos. Sumerian revival is riding Gilgamesh's spike.
items.why: Seven gates = seven scenes. Stripping, death, the fly, Dumuzi's substitution — a complete 8-minute tragedy.
items.gap: Academic tellings only. This is the rare myth that is already structured like our scene list.

items.title: Every Palace From Greece to Egypt Burned in One Generation
items.hook: In the same lifetime, Mycenae, Ugarit, Hattusa and a dozen other palaces went dark. The last clay tablets from Ugarit say the ships are on the horizon. Then the writing stops.
items.demand: Sea Peoples + Late Bronze Age collapse is a steady education query with spikes whenever a new paper lands. Wendigoon-adjacent audience already watches collapse content.
items.why: Maps, burning palaces, unread Linear B, a letter that never arrived. Investigation voice, not sermon. The honest ending is: we still do not know which cause was first.
items.gap: Documentaries run 50 minutes and hedge. A 12-minute 'here is the last letter' cut does not exist in this style.

items.topic: The Year Without a Summer — Tambora, 1816
items.title: A Volcano in Indonesia Invented Frankenstein
items.hook: Mount Tambora killed so much sunlight that 1816 had no summer. Crops failed from China to New England. In a rain-trapped villa on Lake Geneva, Mary Shelley sat down and invented a man who should not have been alive.
items.demand: Year Without a Summer + Tambora is a reliable curiosity query; Frankenstein search is enormous and seasonal. The causal chain between them is rarely the title.
items.why: Ash, red snow, famine, Byron, the villa, the creature. One cause, one lesson, cinematic weather.
items.gap: Climate explainers and Frankenstein biographies are separate videos. The join is the video.

items.title: The Doctors Ordered Them to Dance, and They Danced Until They Died
items.hook: In Strasbourg, a woman started dancing in the street and would not stop. Within a month, hundreds had joined. The physicians' prescription was more dancing. Some of them danced themselves to death.
items.demand: Evergreen weird-history search (ergot, mass psychogenic illness, 'unexplained'). Short, complete, visually grotesque in a painterly way — perfect 8-minute Dark Vault.
items.why: One city, one month, one medical mistake. Opens cold, never resolves cleanly (ergot vs. hysteria vs. stress), which is the Dark Vault ending.
items.gap: List-video fodder ('10 weirdest plagues'). A single-incident investigation with a thesis is open.
